newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says 3 countries join EU in whiskey inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Chile says 3 countries join EU in whiskey inquiry.

text.p: Mexico, Peru and the United States have joined the European Union in a World Trade Organization inquiry into Chilean taxes on whiskey and other spirits, a senior Chilean government official said Wednesday.
Chilean Agriculture Minister Carlos Mladinic said the three countries had added their names to the inquiry. But he said their participation was not viewed as an unfriendly act.

"They have indeed joined the consultations. This is a normal mechanism to resolve trade disputes, and it does not imply an aggressive attitude by any of the countries involved," Mladinic told reporters.

The dispute centers on a 70 percent tax imposed since the 1970s on sales of whiskey. A 25 percent tax is levied on sales of spirits with less alcohol, notably pisco, a clear brandy made in Chile. The pisco industry is a major employer in parts of northern Chile.

The European Union has complained that the tax protects pisco producers unfairly to the detriment of imported whiskey, including scotch. Whiskey makers from the United States, Canada and elsewhere have also complained, but Britain has taken the lead in demanding an end to the tax, which it considers a non-tariff trade barrier.

President Eduardo Frei's government has proposed a gradual reduction in the tax, hoping to bring it in line with WTO standards. But European Commission Vice President Leon Brittan said during a visit to Chile in April that the reduction would "not correspond to our complaint and will not resolve the dispute."
Peru has a related dispute with Chile over the name pisco, which each country claims as its own.

The whiskey-tax row has escalated at a time when Chile is facing a fresh trade dispute with the United States. Salmon producers from the U.S. states of Maine and Oregon have filed a dumping complaint with the U.S. Commerce Department against eight Chilean companies.
Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia was due to travel to Washington over the weekend to discuss the salmon complaint and other trade issues with U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley.
